title: Two Pots on the Windowsill
story: The class compared two pots of basil on the same windowsill, giving one extra water and leaving the other on the usual schedule. After ten days the wetter plant had yellow leaves, while the other stayed green. Their teacher said too much water can harm roots just as dryness can. The students recorded both results and agreed the next test should give both pots equal light.

vocabulary.definition: Looked at two things to see how they differed.
The flat shelf along the bottom of a window.
A planned pattern for when something is done.
The parts of a plant that grow under the soil.

quiz.question: How many pots of basil did the class compare?
options: Two
Ten
One
Four
quiz.explanation: The class compared two pots of basil on the same windowsill.
quiz.supportingSentence: The class compared two pots of basil on the same windowsill, giving one extra water and leaving the other on the usual schedule.

quiz.question: What do the yellow leaves suggest about the extra water?
options: The extra water was bad for that plant
The wetter plant needed still more water
The green plant had been kept in the dark
The windowsill was too dry for both pots
quiz.correctAnswer: The extra water was bad for that plant
quiz.explanation: The plant that got extra water turned yellow, while the other stayed green.
quiz.supportingSentence: After ten days the wetter plant had yellow leaves, while the other stayed green.

quiz.question: Why keep the light equal in the next test?
options: So light will not be the reason for any difference
So one pot can sit in a dark cupboard
So the class can stop writing results
So both pots can be given extra water
quiz.correctAnswer: So light will not be the reason for any difference
quiz.explanation: Equal light means a later difference cannot be blamed on one pot getting more light.
quiz.supportingSentence: The students recorded both results and agreed the next test should give both pots equal light.

quiz.question: What does harm mean in this story?
options: Cause damage
Give an equal amount
Write a result down
Stay green and healthy
quiz.explanation: The teacher says too much water can harm roots, meaning it can damage them.
quiz.supportingSentence: Their teacher said too much water can harm roots just as dryness can.

quiz.question: Why did the students write down both results?
options: So they would have a record of what each pot did
So they could throw the green plant away
So the teacher would add more water
So the usual schedule would stay secret
quiz.correctAnswer: So they would have a record of what each pot did
quiz.explanation: They recorded both results in order to keep what they had observed.
quiz.supportingSentence: The students recorded both results and agreed the next test should give both pots equal light.
